title: Sales Enablement: Positioning & Messaging, Competitive Briefs, Pitch Decks, Pricing Guidance, Case Studies, Security FAQ
author: Ava Martinez
summary: This document is the canonical sales enablement reference for Redwood Inference covering positioning and messaging, competitive differentiation, a standardized pitch deck outline, pricing guidance for enterprise prospects, representative case studies, and a security FAQ tailored for prospect conversations. Use this page in customer-facing sales cycles (AE, SE, Solutions Engineering) and for internal training.
positioning_and_messaging:
Objective: Provide concise, repeatable messaging for AEs and SEs to articulate Redwood's value to engineering and platform buyer personas.

Core positioning: Redwood Inference is a developer-first inference platform that makes LLM-powered features predictable, cost-effective, and production-ready across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments. We optimize for latency, reliability, and unit economics, while offering a consistent API and observability tools that reduce operational risk.

Key customer problems we solve:
- Unpredictable inference costs and token economics at scale.
- Variability in latency and reliability across cloud GPUs and model variants.
- Operational burden of model serving (rollouts, KV caching, quantization, tracing).
- Compliance and data residency needs for regulated workloads.

Top-line messages (elevator pitch):
- For engineering teams building LLM features, Redwood Inference provides a single runtime and control plane that makes inference predictable, fast, and cost-efficient without requiring teams to manage model-serving complexity.

Three-tiered messaging by persona:
- Engineering/ML Engineers: "Drop-in SDKs, deterministic latency profiles, and built-in batching/caching mean you ship fast and keep unit costs low."
- Platform/Infra Leads: "Dedicated capacity, autoscaling policies, and workload-aware routing deliver predictable throughput and compliance controls."
- Product/Revenue Leaders: "Lower per-session cost and consistent latency lead to better UX and improved unit economics for LLM features."

Proof points and metrics to cite in conversations:
- Average p99 generation latency reductions of 20-40% vs unoptimized endpoints (internal benchmarks).
- Typical per-token cost savings 15-45% from caching + intelligent batching + quantization recommendations on production workloads.
- Customer examples: reduced inference costs by ~30% and improved throughput 2-3x for a mid-market SaaS customer (see case study below).
competitive_briefs:
Objective: Equip reps with brief, actionable comparisons vs key competitors (managed LLM APIs, cloud managed endpoints, self-hosted inference runtimes). Use these points when buyers ask comparison questions.

Competitor: Major managed LLM API provider (M-Large)
- Where Redwood wins: predictable unit economics, on-prem/VPC private deployment option, and transparent performance profiles for curated open models.
- Where competitor wins: broader model catalog and aggressive pricing for SMB bursty use-cases.
- Rebuttal guidance: emphasize cost controls (batching, caching) and our Dedicated contracts for predictable pricing and SLA-backed capacity. Offer a short TCO example for the buyer's expected QPS.

Competitor: Cloud managed endpoints (C-Cloud Endpoint)
- Where Redwood wins: specialized inference runtime optimizations (attention kernels, KV management), and unified experience across hosted/dedicated/private. Better observability and routing policies for mixed-latency workloads.
- Where competitor wins: deeper integration with adjacent cloud services, native IAM/marketplace flows.
- Rebuttal guidance: highlight portability (no vendor lock-in), private deployment options, and our readiness for regulated workloads. We provide clear migration/runbook templates.

Competitor: Self-hosted inference stack / OSS runtimes (OSS-Runtime)
- Where Redwood wins: managed operational controls, SRE-grade SLAs, rollout tooling (canaries, automatic fallback), and cost optimization without hiring inference ops.
- Where competitor wins: lower software license cost at very large scale and full control over infra.
- Rebuttal guidance: position Redwood as the fastest path to production-grade inference with lower total cost of ownership when accounting for engineering time. Offer an ROI worksheet during POC.

Competitive battlecard quick facts (one-liners):
- "Redwood provides consistent p99 latency SLOs with autoscaling and reserved capacity, ideal for production apps."
- "We reduce per-token spend with caching and quantization suggestions tied to your workload."
- "Private deployments with KMS/HSM integrations for regulated industries."
pitch_deck_outline:
Use this standardized pitch deck outline for AE + SE presentations. Keep decks targeted to the persona and decision stage. Include 8-12 slides for discovery/solution fit; 12-18 slides for deeper technical/enterprise reviews.

Suggested slide flow (core):
1. Title + meeting objective + attendees
2. Quick Redwood overview (one-liner + mission)
3. Customer pain summary (mirror buyer language)
4. Solution overview: Redwood platform modes (Hosted API, Dedicated, Private)
5. How it works at a high level (serving runtime, routing, caching)
6. Key differentiators (performance, cost controls, unified runtime)
7. Reference architecture (hosted vs dedicated vs private)
8. Observability & ops: Console screenshots + tracing/cost breakdowns
9. Pricing & capacity options (high-level)
10. Case study: similar customer (metrics + ROI)
11. Security & compliance summary (KMS, VPC, audit logs)
12. Next steps & recommended trial/POC plan

Technical appendix (optional slides):
- Performance benchmarks and p99/p50 numbers for typical sequence lengths
- Quantization profiles and supported model families
- Autoscaling policies and example SLO configuration
- Runbook snippet for private deployment onboarding

Deck tips:
- Always customize slide 3 (customer pain) and slide 10 (case study) to be directly relevant.
- Bring an SE for enterprise technical reviews and share the appendix PDF ahead of the call.
- Prepare a short TCO comparison tailored to the buyer's traffic profile to include on slide 9.
pricing_guidance:
Objective: Provide AEs with guidelines to price Redwood solutions during discovery and for initial proposals. This is high-level guidance; finance/partnerships should be engaged for final quotes.

High-level pricing components:
- Hosted API: usage-based (per-token generation + per-embedding unit) with tiered discounts at volume commitments.
- Dedicated: monthly reserved capacity (GPU-hour commits) + overage rates and optional burst capacity.
- Private: platform licensing fee (annual or multi-year) + deployment support and optional managed services.

Guidance for quoting during discovery:
1. Understand expected QPS, average sequence length, and concurrency.
2. Ask about latency SLOs and acceptable degradation; those drive Dedicated recommendations.
3. Estimate token volume for 30/90/365 day horizons and run a cost model with/without caching. We provide a TCO worksheet (link in related pages).

Discounting guardrails:
- Standard self-serve customers get published rates; pipeline-enterprise deals require finance approval for >20% discount or multi-year commitments.
- Commitments for Dedicated: encourage 12-36 month terms for deeper discounts and capacity guarantees.

POC/Trial pricing:
- Offer short-term trial credits (hosted API) for proof-of-concept. For enterprise POCs with private/Dedicated, use a time-limited pilot contract with capped usage to control risk.

Value-based upsell signals:
- Sustained high QPS with predictable peaks -> Recommend Dedicated reserved capacity.
- Strict compliance or data residency -> Recommend Private deployment + enterprise license.
- Large embedding workloads -> Recommend volume tier discounts or committed-embedding bundles.
case_studies:
Include short, anonymized case studies for customer conversations and decks. Use numbers where permitted and anonymize customer names when confidentiality applies.

Case Study A: Mid-market SaaS - Conversational Support Assistant
- Problem: Latency spikes and high per-session cost impacting live chat UX during peak hours.
- Solution: Migrated to Redwood Dedicated with autoscaling + KV prefix caching and model quantization suggestions.
- Outcome: 30% reduction in per-session inference cost, 2.5x throughput improvement at peak, and p99 latency improved from 900ms to 320ms.
- Timeline: 8-week pilot to production.

Case Study B: Regulated FinTech - Document Classification & Redaction
- Problem: Data residency and auditability requirements prevented using hosted public APIs.
- Solution: Private deployment in customer VPC, integrated with customer KMS and audit logging. Provided rollout policy and SLOs for batch classification.
- Outcome: Compliant deployment within 12 weeks, audit readiness for SOC2/ISO review, and predictable monthly costs via a platform license.

Case Study C: Marketplace Company - Personalization Embeddings
- Problem: High embedding costs at scale and slow indexing pipelines.
- Solution: Implemented intelligent batching and cached embedding retrieval; recommended a quantized model variant for bulk indexing.
- Outcome: 40% cost reduction on nightly indexing jobs and reduced downstream recommendation latency by 18%.
security_faq:
Purpose: Field common security questions from prospects during sales cycles. Use the answers below as canonical responses; defer to Security & Compliance for detailed or unusual requests.

Q: Where does Redwood store customer data?
A: For Hosted mode, request/response metadata and logs are stored in region-specific storage with encryption at rest (AES-256). Customers can opt for private deployments (VPC or on-prem) if they require full control over data residency.

Q: How is data encrypted in transit and at rest?
A: TLS 1.2+ for all in-transit communications. At-rest encryption using cloud provider KMS by default; for Private deployments we support customer-managed KMS and HSM integrations.

Q: Do you support customer-managed keys?
A: Yes. Private deployments and Enterprise plans support customer-managed keys via KMS/HSM integrations and audited key usage.

Q: What audit logs and monitoring do you provide?
A: Audit logs include authentication events, admin actions (deployments, model rollouts), and API usage traces. These are retained per the agreed retention schedule and can be exported to the customer's SIEM for longer-term retention.

Q: How do you handle model updates and rollbacks?
A: We provide controlled rollout mechanisms (canaries, A/B testing) and automatic fallback policies that redirect traffic to a safe model variant if error rates or latency regressions exceed thresholds. All rollouts are logged for auditability.

Q: What compliance certifications do you have?
A: Redwood maintains SOC 2 Type II readiness and a roadmap for ISO 27001. For customer-specific compliance, we provide evidence packages and support during audits as part of enterprise engagements.

Q: Is customer prompt/data used to train models?
A: By default, customer data is not used to improve public model weights. For hosted customers who opt in to data use programs, we provide explicit agreements. Private deployments keep data fully within customer-controlled environments.

Q: How do you secure private deployments (networking)?
A: Private deployments are deployed within customer VPCs or on-prem networks using least-privilege IAM roles, VPC peering or private links, and hardened baselines for host OS and container runtimes. We provide onboarding runbooks and an audit checklist.

Contact for security requests: security@redwoodinference.internal (for internal use) and your designated CSM/AE for prospect-facing coordination.
recommended_playbook_steps:
Use this short playbook during an enterprise opportunity: 
1. Discovery: Capture QPS, sequence length, latency SLOs, compliance needs, and decision timeline.
2. Align offering: Recommend Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private and propose a POC scope (30/60/90 days).
3. TCO: Generate a TCO model with caching assumptions and present a comparison vs the incumbent.
4. Security review: Share Security FAQ and related evidence packages; coordinate a security review call if requested.
5. Pilot: Offer trial credits or a time-limited Dedicated pilot with clear success metrics (latency, cost, throughput).
6. Commercial: Draft an MSA + SOW for Dedicated/Private deals; involve legal and finance for any non-standard terms.
7. Onboarding: Handover to Solutions Engineering and Customer Success with a runbook and acceptance criteria.
